correctness.rationale: Each codeword difference from a cube vertex has block parity T or T-complement. Blockwise Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the square of the Euclidean norm from below by lambda^2 W_T+(1-lambda)^2(S-W_T); independent uniform one-bit flips in prescribed odd blocks attain equality with lambda=(S-W_T)/S. Strict convexity gives the unique projection. The residual-variance identity and sign nonvanishing at every coordinate of every noncode cube vertex prove no nonvertex farthest points. Maximizing the resulting reciprocal subset product gives all equality cases and counts. Exact rational KKT certificates exhaustively checked all binary vertices/codewords in ten listed small profiles; independent SLSQP convex-combination QP corroborated four profiles. These finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The parity-lift of the binary repetition code is a canonical simultaneous-check 0/1-polytope. The theorem gives exact Euclidean cube-approximation error for every block-length profile, unique projections of all cube vertices, a complete arithmetic farthest-point classification, a dominant-block localization law, and an exact factor-four asymptotic squared-error gain over independently even-constrained block polytopes. This is a motivated metric comparison of simultaneous versus independent parity constraints, not a tiny isolated parameter computation; it makes no unsupported decoding-performance claim.
